## JOURNAL-MOTIVE-R-007 — MAP.md as ambient auto-regenerated file {#journal-motive-r-007}

`.groundwork/motives/<slug>/MAP.md` **shall** exist as a file on disk and **shall** auto-regenerate from the ticket corpus with ledger status overlay after each `journal append`, `journal motive new`, and `journal compile` invocation; it **shall not** require an explicit separate CLI invocation to be current.

- **Why** — A MAP available only on CLI demand is invisible to filesystem-reading tools (Obsidian, IDE file trees, git status, shell glob scripts). The human read path must be ambient — a file that is always present and reflects the last-known state without requiring a separate generation step. A stale or absent MAP.md causes a reader to see old ticket state, potentially acting on superseded work.
- **Fit criterion** — After running `bun bin/journal show --motive <slug>` (read-only), `MAP.md` is still present and unmodified. After running a write command (`journal motive new` on a throwaway motive), `MAP.md` exists in the motive directory with modification time at or after the command's start time. `MAP.md` is generated by `hooks/lib/motive-map.mjs` and written to `<motiveDir>/MAP.md` (source: line 113).
- **Verification**: manual — `ls -la .groundwork/motives/obsidian-native-groundwork/MAP.md` — confirm existence. On a throwaway motive created via `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=/tmp/scratch bun bin/journal motive new test-map`, confirm `MAP.md` is created immediately. Source: `hooks/lib/motive-map.mjs` lines 2, 25, 113; `hooks/journal.mjs` line 402.
- **Criticality**: must
